findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an item (or extend item 1/step 6) that REWRITES the `undecomposed` and `dod_uncertifiable` bullets in both plan_review_verifier.md and plan_review_verifier_agentic.md to enumerate the six new kind names with per-kind selection rules (mirroring the existing ac_unverifiable / divergent_implementation kind bullets), not merely delete the G5 hedge.
evidence: Prompt bullets currently carry only ordinal/HARD-OVERRIDE prose: 'dod_uncertifiable — a definition-of-done / success criterion cannot be certified true. HARD-OVERRIDE' and 'undecomposed — the plan is a flat, undecomposed unit ... HARD-OVERRIDE' — no kind vocabulary.

By contrast the already-converted axes co-locate each kind name + meaning in the SAME prompt (ac_unverifiable lines 78-82; divergent_implementation lines 88-106 spell out contradicts_reality / omits_required_site / incomplete_enumeration with examples).

Item 1 scope is only 'Delete the inert G5-suppressor hedge from both prompts and the undecomposed description'; step 6 preserves the 'success criterion' phrasing but adds no kind vocabulary to the prompt bullets.
These fields are EMITTED by the LLM (verify_models.py PlanSeverityAttrs, decide.impact_plan '...emitted by verify.plan_review_verification_model'), so the reviewer must be told which kind to choose.
findings.finding: Items 2-3 redefine `undecomposed` and `dod_uncertifiable` as closed kind sets emitted by the plan-review verifier LLM, but the plan only directs DELETING the G5 hedge from the two reviewer prompts (item 1) — it never directs ADDING the six new kind names and their pick-this-kind decision rules to the `undecomposed`/`dod_uncertifiable` bullets in plan_review_verifier.md and plan_review_verifier_agentic.md.
scenarios: The verifier LLM must grade a plan that bundles independently-shippable slices but has no way to know whether to emit `bundles_separable_slices` (advisory 0.55) vs `missing_required_child` (floors 0.85) — the exact low-vs-high distinction the migration exists to make deterministic.
Post-landing the Literal model rejects `low|medium|high`, but the prompt still implies an ordinal grade, so the model emits a stale or arbitrary label and the finding validates as none/errors.
findings.suggested_fix: In item 1/step 6, replace each ordinal bullet with a closed-kind bullet listing the kinds and which floor vs contribute 0.55, exactly as ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation are already presented in the prompts (prompt lines 78-106), and preserve the pinned 'success criterion' phrasing.

findings.finding: Step 6's rewrite inventory for `test_impact_plan.py` names three ordinal-keyed cases for the two axes but omits `test_override_survives_self_revealing_amplifier` (line 107-114), which keys on `{"undecomposed": "medium", ...}` and asserts `impact_plan(attrs) >= 0.85`. findings.finding: Item 4's decision-margin telemetry records `impact_sev - block_threshold`, but the gate's actual BLOCK decision compares `priority (= validity × impact) >= block_threshold` (decide.py pass3_decide), not `impact_sev`. `impact_sev` is a pre-amplifier/pre-floor local inside impact_plan and is not the final impact scalar, nor is it currently returned to the sidecar (only `impact` and `priority` are). The recorded quantity therefore does not represent the decision margin it is named for.
findings.location: What section item 4 ('Decision-margin telemetry'); Steps step 3; AC line 'The sidecar records a per-finding decision margin'
findings.suggested_fix: Record `priority - block_threshold` (both already available in pass3_decide's return dict) as the decision margin, and have the margin test assert that value against a known priority/threshold pair. If a pre-amplifier signal is genuinely wanted, name and document it distinctly rather than calling it the decision margin.
